analysis: The only changed file is a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Tools/FlintNativeProtocolTests.swift. It adds a test at head lines 209-226 and one assertion at head line 267. The test is maskCacheKeysIdentifyIdenticalMasksAndOptIntoChaining. It checks that FlintNativeProtocolConstraint exposes allowsChainedDecode and maskCacheKey(state:remainingTokens:). It requires nil keys for zero remaining tokens and for out-of-range states. It requires that identical keys always correspond to identical allowed-token masks. The assertion at line 267 requires a nil mask key once the state pool is exhausted, so that fail-closed state cannot be cached as a normal mask. These tests only constrain behavior and add no runtime attack surface. They concern tool-call and think-channel protocol enforcement in TB-007 inference (the model-output protocol constraint). They do not touch the wire contract, attestation, keys, authorization, or cache storage (T-041). The production implementation of maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode is not in the supplied evidence. The next review pass should confirm that maskCacheKey does not collapse distinct masks, for example by ignoring the remainingTokens boundary, the parallel-call cardinality, or the tool schema. It should also confirm that chained decode cannot bypass the per-token constraint checks. This pass cannot verify either point from tests alone. No security regression is identified in the supplied test changes.
